Annotation.String: This action set the Power Limiting value for standalone servers, where a user may enter a Power Limiting value of the chassis.

This action sets the Power Limiting value for standalone servers, where a user may enter a Power Limiting value of the chassis. This command includes Chassis-level Power Capping, Sled-level Power Capping, and Emergency Power Capping
This parameter specifies the power limiting value in watts.
This parameter specifies the power limiting value in watts, with the least significant byte first.
This parameter defines the power limiting status for the chassis enclosure.
This parameter defines the power limiting status for the chassis enclosure.
This parameter specifies the action to take when the power limit is reached.
This parameter specifies the action to take when the power limit is reached, such as throttling via PROCHOT or software mechanisms.
This parameter defines the sled-level power capping exception.
This parameter defines the exception policy for sled-level power capping, indicating whether to follow its own sled-level power capping or chassis-level power capping.
This parameter specifies the emergency action policy for chassis power capping.
This parameter specifies the emergency action policy for chassis power capping, such as doing nothing, throttling via PROCHOT, throttling via software, or powering off.
This parameter defines the emergency action policy for sled power capping.
This parameter defines the emergency action policy for sled power capping, indicating whether to follow chassis policy, throttle via PROCHOT, throttle via software, or power off.

Power capping is enabled.
No action is taken, this value is a placeholder.
This value is reserved and does not correspond to any specific power capping mechanism. It is essentially a placeholder and should not be used for actual power capping actions
Throttling via PROCHOT (Processor Hot) is a hardware-based mechanism that ensures immediate response to thermal events, providing a reliable way to manage power and thermal conditions.
Throttling via PROCHOT (Processor Hot) is a hardware-based mechanism that ensures immediate response to thermal events, providing a reliable way to manage power and thermal conditions
Throttling via software mechanisms like NM (Node Manager) or APML (Advanced Platform Management Link) allows for more flexible and granular control over power management.

Software-based mechanisms like NM (Node Manager) or APML (Advanced Platform Management Link) provide dynamic and flexible control over power consumption, allowing for more sophisticated power management strategies.
No action is taken, this value is a placeholder.
This value is reserved and does not correspond to any specific power capping mechanism. It is essentially a placeholder and should not be used for actual power capping actions.
Follow its own sled-level power capping.

When this value is set, the sled will follow its own power capping rules and limits independently of the chassis-level power capping. This means that each sled within the chassis can have its own power capping settings, allowing for more granular control over power consumption at the sled level.
Follow chassis-level power capping.

When this value is set, the sled will adhere to the power capping rules and limits defined at the chassis level. This means that the power capping settings applied to the entire chassis will also apply to each sled within it, ensuring uniform power management across all sleds.
Specifies that no action is taken for emergency power capping at the chassis level.
Specifies that no action is taken for emergency power capping at the chassis level.
Throttle via PROCHOT (Processor Hot).
Specifies that the processor will be throttled using the PROCHOT (Processor Hot) signal to reduce power consumption during emergency power capping at the chassis level.
Throttle via software mechanism NM (Node Manager).
Specifies that the processor will be throttled using a software mechanism, such as Node Manager NM (Node Manager), to reduce power consumption during emergency power capping at the chassis level.
Power Off.
Specifies that the system will be powered off to reduce power consumption during emergency power capping at the chassis level.
Follow chassis policy.
Specifies that the sled will follow the emergency power capping actions defined at the chassis level.

Indicates whether the input current limit is enabled.

This property specifies whether the input current limit functionality is enabled for the system. When set to true, the system will enforce the input current limit to ensure stability and prevent overcurrent conditions. This property is crucial for maintaining system integrity and preventing potential hardware damage.
This property specifies the value in milliAmps (mA) to use in Set SPA calculations, with a default value of 0. It is only valid if the GridChassisICLEnabled Bit 0 is set to 1.

This property specifies the value in milliAmps (mA) to use in Set SPA calculations, with a default value of 0. It is only valid if the GridChassisICLEnabled Bit 0 is set to 1. This is a read-only property that can only be set by the Chassis Manager (CM) and applies to Lake Austin only.

This property specifies the Bulk Voltage Modulation (BVM) setting for PSUs.

This property specifies the Bulk Voltage Modulation (BVM) setting for Power Supply Units (PSUs). It can be set to 0 or 1, with a default value of 1. This property applies to Hubble and Lake Austin systems only.
This property enables the Power Adapter Cable Support.

This property enables the Power Adapter Cable Support, such as for the C19-C14 cable. A value of 0 disables it, while a value greater than 0 enables it for the specified amp limit (e.g., 0Ch = 12 Amps). The default value is 0. This value is read-only and set to 0Ch when a PSU with a specific part number is inserted.
